newsitem.title: UK: British minister in N.Irish parade talks.
newsitem.headline: British minister in N.Irish parade talks.

text.p: Britain's Northern Ireland minister Mo Mowlam visited sectarian flashpoints in the troubled province on Wednesday for talks aimed at defusing tension over annual parades by pro-British Protestants.

Government sources said Mowlam went to the mainly Roman Catholic village of Dunloy, where violence flared during a banned parade last Sunday. She also met residents in Portadown's Catholic Garvaghy Road, which was the centre of province-wide clashes a year ago over a disputed march.
Members of the Protestant Orange Order, known as Orangemen, say their traditional parades are held to celebrate their religion and their loyalty to the British Crown.
Catholics say the parades commemorate ancient Protestant victories over the native Irish and are intended as displays of Protestant domination over them.
Concern about possible clashes in this year's "marching season" has cast a shadow over struggling peace efforts in Northern Ireland.
Mowlam met senior leaders of the 200-year-old Orange Order, which has tens of thousands of members, at her official residence of Hillsborough Castle, south of Belfast, on Tuesday night.
They were from County Armagh, where Portadown is one of the main towns.

Two Catholics were killed last July when clashes swept the province. Violence flared when police tried to stop a controversial Orange Order march at Drumcree near Garvaghy Road but later allowed the Protestants to walk past Catholic housing estates.
A spokesman for the Northern Ireland Office said Mowlam's meetings were "being undertaken in response to requests received from the organisations".

News of the meetings emerged as leaders of Sinn Fein, the political wing of Irish Republican Army guerrillas, prepared for their first meeting with British officials since the collapse of an IRA truce in February 1996.
The IRA, supported by some of the province's minority Catholics, wants to end British sovereignty and unite the province with neighbouring Catholic Ireland.
